reason: Reviewed the complete A/B batch against the approved GR03 scope and actual suppliers. Scope is sufficient; page-local proof and claim defects need the single local repair.

findings.reason: Part 3 invokes proper time for a timelike geodesic without requiring it to be future-directed, although the supplied worldline definition assigns proper time only to future timelike curves. Part 4's iff is false for constant geodesics, which the supplied geodesic definition includes: every reparametrization of a constant curve remains geodesic. Add the future-direction hypothesis and separate the constant case or require a regular geodesic for the converse.
Step 5.1 only constructs an increasing subdivision from 0 to t0, so it does not prove smooth dependence when t0<0. Give the corresponding decreasing-time construction.

Step 2.3 uses maximal-geodesic uniqueness to assert chart coordinates u(γ(t))=t k, but the inverse exponential chart only returns vectors in W. Explicitly restrict the argument to the connected passage through p in the normal chart and justify that the radial vector remains in W there.

In the converse, D_tγ' is only continuous for the stated C2 curve, so Z=g#(D_tγ') need not be smooth; [L7] does not justify calling it smooth, and the resulting H is not shown C2. Choose a C2 variation field from smooth chart components that pairs positively with the acceleration near t0, or supply sufficient regularity.

In step 1.3 the signature convention gives Q(T*)≤0 for a future causal limit, not Q(T*)≥0; the limit may also be zero. In steps 3.1–3.2, [L3] applies to an observer and a future causal vector, and its reverse Cauchy–Schwarz claim is for unit timelike vectors; normalize and, in 3.1, swap the pairing arguments explicitly. In the equality proof, v(1)/ρ(1) is not shown to lie in W; normalize ρ(1)=1 and take v0=v(1).

The postulate assumes a physical worldline is a geodesic but does not require its domain to be maximal. The proof establishes equality on common domains and that both worldlines are restrictions of the unique maximal geodesic; it does not establish that each physical worldline is maximal. Replace that assertion with the restriction/unique-extension claim.
For φ=λx¹ the stated list of nonzero symbols is incomplete: Γ¹₂₂=Γ¹₃₃=−λ and Γ²₁₂=Γ²₂₁=Γ³₁₃=Γ³₃₁=λ are also nonzero. Correct the list and the accompanying vanishing claim.

The example asserts without hypotheses or proof that every curve satisfying ∇_{β'}β'=fβ' with continuous f is the image of a geodesic. State the regularity and nonzero-velocity conditions and prove the reparametrization, or restrict the claim to the displayed β.

The claim does not specify whether equality of geodesic images is local or global, while step 2.2 only constructs h on intervals where 2v⁰s+C>0 and cannot reparametrize an entire line domain in general. State the local unparametrized-path scope and define “regular curve” or give its exact conditions.
